note_sections.t: Clinical reassessment prompted by a PSA increase to 4.1 ng/mL alongside a previously confirmed positive biopsy result.

A 72-year-old retired bus driver, widowed, entered the workup for a PSA elevation in mid-2023, a value that has now climbed to 4.1 ng/mL. He resides in an assisted-living facility situated over 90 minutes from the hospital, prompting a preference for telephone monitoring when clinically suitable. Despite his years, his lifestyle remains vigorous; he jogs 5 km three times each week and experiences only slight urinary bother, scoring a 7 on the IPSS. Tobacco use ceased entirely in 2021 after accumulating 10 pack-years, and he avoids alcohol. No comorbidities are present, and he takes no medications. Unrelated recent medical encounters include a dermatology visit for actinic keratosis monitoring and a completed six-session physiotherapy regimen addressing mechanical lower back pain. He maintains baseline functionality without systemic complaints.

DRE — texture: uniformly smooth; mobility: unrestricted; asymmetry: absent. The prostate appears symmetrically benign with no palpable nodules, confirming a normal digital rectal assessment. General inspection shows a well-nourished gentleman free of acute distress, maintaining stable vital signs and clear breath sounds. Abdominal palpation yields no masses or organomegaly, remaining entirely unremarkable.
